prompt: This is an art-direction redesign for Yorimichi, a stylised Japanese autumn exploration game made in Unreal. Image 1 is a real, unretouched screenshot of the game as it is now. Repaint THE SAME VIEW from the same camera, keeping the layout, street grid, terrain, building positions, sea and sky composition, but redesigned to the standard of a polished commercial stylised game (think Ghibli-inspired, hand-crafted, cosy, dense and lived-in): textured materials with soft hand-painted detail instead of flat untextured colour, coherent warm autumn palette, gentle afternoon sunlight. It must stay a believable real-time game frame built from meshes, textures and foliage, not a loose illustration. No text, no UI, no watermark. A main shopping street. The buildings are decent but the street is an extremely wide, empty grey asphalt slab and the materials are flat untextured colour. Redesign: narrower worn asphalt with patching and painted markings, granite curbs, textured stone-tile sidewalks, timber with visible wood grain, plaster walls with subtle grime, tiled roofs with texture, utility poles with overhead wires, vending machines, potted plants, bicycles, noren curtains, hanging signs, paper lanterns, street trees, a few people. Dense, lived-in, cosy Japanese town street.
